Security is core to Phantom’s product and the trust millions of users place in us. We’re building an AI-native security team that aggressively uses AI to expand the speed, depth, and reach of our work—from code review and threat modeling to vulnerability discovery and security automation. We’re looking for strong security engineers with high agency who can identify the risks that matter, build practical solutions, and take ownership from initial discovery through verified remediation.

This is a hands-on, high-impact role spanning architecture, source code, testing, and production systems across Phantom’s mobile, web, and backend products. You’ll work directly with engineering and product teams, lead complex security initiatives, and build capabilities that scale across the company. At the Staff level, you’ll set technical direction and raise the bar for how Phantom designs, builds, and ships secure products.

This role is fully remote and open to candidates based in the US, UK and Canada.

Responsibilities

  • Product Security Ownership: Partner with engineering teams to identify and address security risks across Phantom’s mobile applications, web products, APIs, and backend services.

  • Architecture and Threat Modeling: Lead security reviews for new products and major architectural changes, with particular attention to authorization boundaries, sensitive data, transaction integrity, key material, and third-party integrations.

  • Secure Product Development: Embed practical security controls into the software development lifecycle, from design and implementation through testing, release, and production operation.

  • Code Review and Security Testing: Perform AI assisted security code reviews and targeted testing of high-risk features. Build repeatable approaches that help find vulnerabilities before they reach production.

  • Security Tooling: Develop and improve tooling that gives engineers fast, actionable security feedback without creating unnecessary friction. Use automation and AI-assisted workflows where they materially improve coverage or speed.

  • Software Supply Chain Security: Harden CI/CD, build, and release systems against supply chain threats, including dependency risk, secrets exposure, build provenance, artifact integrity, and compromised developer or automation workflows.

  • Vulnerability Management: Triage findings from internal testing, researchers, bug bounty submissions, and third-party assessments. Work with owners to determine real-world impact and drive issues through verified remediation.

  • Incident Response: Support the investigation of product security incidents and suspicious activity. Turn lessons from incidents into durable improvements to product architecture, detection, and engineering standards.

  • Technical Leadership: Establish product security patterns and expectations across engineering. At the Staff level, lead ambiguous, cross-functional initiatives and influence architecture beyond any single product team.

  • 5+ years of experience in product security, application security, security engineering, or software engineering, including experience operating at a senior or staff level.

  • Strong understanding of web, mobile, API, and distributed-system security, including authentication, authorization, session management, cryptography, and common vulnerability classes.

  • Hands-on experience building or applying AI-assisted security tooling to test applications and APIs, combining automated analysis with source-code review and manual validation.

  • Demonstrated ability to review production code in one or more languages such as TypeScript, JavaScript, Rust, Python and Go.

  • Experience securing software supply chains and CI/CD systems, including dependencies, build infrastructure, secrets, artifacts, signing, and release integrity.

  • Experience threat modeling complex products and translating security risks into concrete engineering requirements.

  • Strong judgment when evaluating exploitability, business impact, and appropriate remediation.

  • Track record of partnering effectively with engineering and product teams while maintaining a high security bar.

  • Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain technical risk to both engineers and non-security stakeholders.

Platform security is foundational to protecting Phantom and the systems our users rely on. We’re hiring a Senior Platform Security Engineer to own and improve security across our AWS and Kubernetes environments. You’ll work directly with infrastructure and engineering teams to secure the control planes, identities, workloads, and deployment systems behind our most critical products.

We’re building an AI-native security team that aggressively uses AI to expand the speed, depth, and reach of our work.   • Identity and Access: Design least-privilege access models for engineers, services, and automation. Build scoped, auditable, and time-bound access paths for sensitive production systems.

  • Experience designing or securing mission-critical systems where compromise, excessive privilege, or loss of availability could have significant customer or business impact.

  • Experience securing CI/CD and software supply chains, including GitHub Actions or similar systems, build runners, workload federation, artifacts, and production deployment paths.

  • Ability to write production-quality code or automation in a language such as TypeScript, Python, Go, or Rust.

  • Clear communication and a strong track record of partnering with infrastructure and engineering teams while maintaining a high security bar.

Your support system

You'll report to Katie Swett Miller, our Chief Product Officer and collaborate closely with Engineering, Design, Data, Marketing, Success, and Sales teams.   • Clear written and verbal communication

  • Bonus if you have Publishing or content creation expertise

  • 6-9+ years in product management with significant ownership of a core, revenue-driving product area.

  • Partnered closely with design to drive long-term vision for a product area, including hands-on involvement in craft and visual polish

  • Comfort balancing short-term wins with long-term vision

  • Systems thinker who builds foundations, not just features

  • Low ego, strong collaborator who influences without authority

  • Customer-focused while maintaining business discipline

Working hours and location

We're 100% remote with team members across the globe, but this role requires consistent overlap with our Engineering, Product, and Design teams across Europe and the U.S. The team has fixed meetings from 10:45–11:45 a.m. Eastern on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays. Cyberhaven is redefining data security by tracing how sensitive data actually moves across endpoints, cloud, SaaS, and now AI tools and agents. Our AI Security team builds the backend systems that give enterprises real-time visibility and control over how their data flows into and out of LLMs, GenAI applications, and autonomous agents. We're looking for a Staff/Principal Backend Software Engineer to be one of the most senior technical voices on this team: an early contributor with substantial influence over the architecture of a new and rapidly evolving product line, solving multiple exciting technical challenges along the way.

About the role

Cyberhaven is building the data security platform for the agentic enterprise. AI agents now read, move, and act on enterprise data at machine speed inside browsers, on endpoints, across SaaS and model providers and the controls built for human users don't see any of it.

Agentic Data Security (ADS) is our answer, and it's a new product line built on top of the DLP and DSPM platform that already makes Cyberhaven the market leader in lineage-based data protection. The data flow graph, the endpoint and browser sensors, and the classification engine are in place and deployed at scale in enterprise environments. What's needed now is a product leader to turn that foundation into a category-defining product.

We're looking for a Director of Product Management to own ADS end to end, strategy, roadmap, positioning, and outcomes. This is a rare combination: the strategic surface area of a new product line with the distribution, telemetry, and enterprise customer base of an established platform. Demand is already ahead of us; every security leader we talk to is being asked what their AI agents are doing with company data, and very few have an answer.

You'll report to the CPO and start as a hands-on, single-threaded owner, growing and leading a PM team as the line scales.

What you'll do

  • Own the ADS product line end to end ; vision, strategy, roadmap, and P&L-level outcomes for the product line.

  • Define what data security means when the actor is an agent, not a person: agent identity and attribution, prompt and context inspection, tool-call and MCP-boundary controls, and enforcement that holds up at machine speed without breaking legitimate work.

  • Translate Cyberhaven's data lineage advantage into agentic use cases, working across the endpoint, browser, and cloud teams to extend the platform.

  • Run the ongoing design partner program and take ADS through beta, and GA turning a charter cohort of enterprise customers into referenceable production deployments and significant revenue traction in the next 6-9 months.

  • Partner with Engineering and Design on a fast release cadence, making the hard scope calls that keep milestones credible.

  • Work directly with Sales, Solutions Engineering, and Customer Experience on packaging, pricing, competitive positioning, and enablement.

  • Be the external voice of ADS; customer briefings, analyst conversations, partner discussions, and industry events.

Who you are

  • 10+ years in product management, including 5+ years leading products in security, with a track record of taking new products from zero to meaningful revenue.

  • Domain depth in one or more of: data security (DLP, DSPM, insider risk), AI/LLM security, or endpoint and browser security. Fluency in how AI agents are actually deployed in enterprises is a strong plus.

  • You've shipped enterprise security products that real security teams operate — you understand detection quality, false positive economics, policy authoring, and why enforcement decisions are hard.

  • Comfortable at both altitudes: you can hold an executive team strategy conversation in the morning and get into detection logic and API design with engineers in the afternoon.

  • Excellent communicator and storyteller; you can make a novel category legible to a CISO, an analyst, and a first-time AE.

  • Located in the US (SF Bay Area preferred).

Zapier's mission is to make automation work for everyone. That mission is funded by revenue — and every dollar of it flows through our Commerce Zone. That means designing the framework and abstractions product teams plug into so they can launch new SKUs without becoming billing experts, building configuration-driven infrastructure for pricing experimentation, and ensuring the platform evolves without foundational rewrites.

This is production-critical, finance-grade infrastructure where correctness is non-negotiable. You'll drive alignment across teams in a space defined by high ambiguity and competing constraints, working closely with Product, Engineering, Finance, and Sales. Hi there!

Zapier is hiring a Manager, Analytics & Strategy to lead our newly formed GTM Analytics team. This team is the central analytics home for Marketing, Sales, RevOps, and Customer Ops, with a mandate to deliver trusted GTM insights, improve the quality and speed of decision-making, and turn repeated questions into durable self-service analytics assets.

You will manage a team of embedded analysts supporting Marketing, Sales, and Support/Customer Ops. Your team will own the day-to-day analytics interface for GTM leaders: funnel reporting, campaign performance, sales and support analytics, forecasting inputs, recurring business reviews, dashboarding, metric definitions, and urgent executive questions.

This is a hands-on analytics leadership role. we're looking for someone who has deep analytics judgment, strong SQL skills, and real GTM domain expertise. You might come from a sales analytics, marketing analytics, revenue analytics, finance, or investment banking environment. The common thread is that you know how to operate with urgency, precision, and a high quality bar, and you are energized by analytics work: scoping ambiguous business questions, pressure-testing numbers, coaching people through complex GTM data questions, and delivering clear recommendations under time pressure.

This is not a pure people-management role. You should be able to lean into advanced analytics, understand core statistical concepts, and guide work on experimentation, forecasting, or segmentation when the work calls for it, but the center of gravity is analytics leadership: trusted reporting, business partnership, analytical QA, stakeholder management, and building a faster, more consistent operating model for GTM data. You should also be AI-native in how you work and excited to make this team a proving ground for self-service analytics, analyst automation, and governed AI-assisted data workflows.

About You

You are a hands-on analytics manager. You have 6+ years of experience in analytics, finance, revenue operations, marketing analytics, sales analytics, business operations, investment banking, or a related field. You have managed analysts or analytics-adjacent teams for at least 3 years, but you are still comfortable rolling up your sleeves to review SQL, inspect a dashboard, pressure-test assumptions, and help frame the answer.

You have strong GTM analytics expertise. You understand how marketing, sales, customer operations, and revenue motions fit together. You have worked with funnels, pipeline, bookings or ARR, campaign performance, sales productivity, support performance, forecasting, attribution, segmentation, or lifecycle analytics. You know how to translate GTM questions into metrics, cuts, cohorts, and recommendations that leaders can act on.

You are excellent with SQL and analytical reasoning. You read and write SQL, reason about grain and joins, identify data quality issues, and coach analysts toward cleaner, more reliable methods. You are comfortable with statistics and advanced analytics concepts such as confidence intervals, incrementality, cohorting, regression, forecasting, and experiment readouts, and you know when to partner with Data Science for heavier modeling work.

You bring finance-grade rigor and urgency. You can operate in a fast-twitch environment where leaders need clear answers quickly.
